whyItMatters: Java adds a step many beginners do not expect: your source code is not run directly. Knowing which stage you are in tells you where to look when something breaks. A message like `cannot find symbol` comes from the compiler, while `ArithmeticException` comes from the running program. It also explains why one compiled program can run on different operating systems.
mentalModel:
Two translators, used at different times. `javac` is the compiler: it reads your `.java` source once and produces bytecode in `.class` files. The JVM (Java Virtual Machine) is the runtime: every time you run the program it loads that bytecode, checks it, and executes it on your actual computer.

The JDK is the developer's toolbox and includes `javac`, the `java` launcher and the JVM. A runtime-only install can run programs but cannot compile them.
syntaxReference:
javac Greeter.java            # compile: produces Greeter.class (bytecode)
java Greeter                  # run: starts the JVM and calls Greeter.main
java Greeter.java             # source-file mode: compile in memory, then run
javac -d out Greeter.java     # write class files into the folder out/
java -cp out Greeter          # run a class found in out/
java --version                # runtime that is first on your PATH
javac --version               # compiler that is first on your PATH

commonMistakes.fix: Use the class name without the extension: `java Greeter`. The launcher looks for a class, not a file.

commonMistakes.mistake: Editing the source and running again without compiling.
commonMistakes.fix: `java Greeter` runs the old `Greeter.class`. Run `javac Greeter.java` after every change, or use source-file mode while learning.

commonMistakes.mistake: Installing only a runtime, then seeing `javac: command not found`.
commonMistakes.fix: Install a JDK, not just a runtime, then check `javac --version`.
`java` searches the current directory and the classpath. Change into the folder that holds the class file, or pass `-cp`.

commonMistakes.mistake: Compiling with a newer JDK than the one that runs the program.
commonMistakes.fix: An `UnsupportedClassVersionError` means the class file is newer than the JVM. Run it on the same or a newer JDK, or compile with `--release` set to the older version.

comparisons.summary: Compile-time errors (syntax and types) appear when you run `javac`, before any output. Run-time errors appear after compilation succeeds, when you run `java`.

supporting.title: Setting up your tools
supporting.body:
Install a current long-term-support JDK (21 or 25) from a vendor build such as Eclipse Temurin, then confirm it with `javac --version`.

Any editor works. An IDE such as IntelliJ IDEA, or VS Code with Java support, adds error highlighting and one-click running, but you should be able to compile from a terminal too.

notes.text: `javac` compiles the source. It prints nothing when compilation succeeds.
A new file appeared: `Greeter.class` holds the bytecode. The source file is unchanged.
`java Greeter` starts the JVM, which loads `Greeter.class` and runs `main`. The command names the class, with no extension.
`bottom` is zero, but the compiler does not track what values variables hold, so this compiles.
The division happens only when the program runs. The JVM throws `ArithmeticException` and the program stops; the stack trace reports the file and line (`Divide.java:5`).
